recipe: 1. Foundry 14.370, the module at 1.2.118; a scene with two Levels, a room on each, stairs (a level-change region) between them, a room of two pieces on the ground floor.
2. As GM, mark the rooms in Room Setup's Rooms tab and set token vision off on the scene.
3. As a player, walk a token up the stairs into the upper room in Daily Life; read the move card's price and the Floors buttons.
4. Try to change floor into a room the stairs do not link; read the refusal and where the token lands.
5. Read on the player's screen which door controls are drawn, and whether the two-piece room is outlined whole.
6. From the player's console try region.setFlag('drpg', 'room', false) on a marked room; read the GM's whisper and the flag after.
l1.settles_if: settled yes when the stairs cost one crossing, the refused change puts the token back on its floor, the fog and buttons follow the floor, only clear or veiled rooms show door controls and a player's mark write is put back or refused; settled no on any room read on another floor or a door control of a dark room

Four comments describe the removed tab as live: room-setup.mjs:1229-1234 says Room Setup 'opens on the Scenes tab whenever its scene holds no room', while roomSetupTab (:403-406) falls back to Rooms; season-setup.mjs:543 says the checklist button 'opens Room Setup on the Scenes tab' over `open: async () => openSeasonSetup()` (:557); room-tile.mjs:53 and room-setup.mjs:378 name the tab as where the hall's facts and the scenes are set.

findings.expected: The line and the comments name Season setup's Scenes part, as the handbook does.

findings.what_happens: The order of MUSIC_STATES puts eclipse above the trial (music-states.mjs:152-154), and the panel's note explains that order with 'an Eclipse during a trial uses the Eclipse's'. findings.evidence: "orderNote": "The first state that applies wins, in the order listed. A Class Trial at night uses the trial's playlists; an Eclipse during a trial uses the Eclipse's."
findings.failure_scenario: A GM setting the playlists reads that an Eclipse during a trial plays the Eclipse's list and plans for a moment the module will not let happen.
findings.expected: The note gives an example the table can reach, or says that an Eclipse and a trial never overlap.
findings.refutation_tried: Read both refusals in clock.mjs setClock and eclipse.mjs's startEclipse check; the only state with both is a clock written before 1.2.74 and kept (clock.mjs:252-256 lets such a write through). The order itself is still true of the code, so this is a text that describes a dead case, not a wrong rule.

l1.what: the room tile and a GM's Foundry windows on a real v14 table
recipe: 1. Foundry 14.370, the module at 1.2.118, Stained Glass; a GM and two players; one room with a picture and words in Room Setup's Description tab.
2. A player walks into the room; read the tile (own room only, picture, words, the chevron); another player's tile stays on their own room.
3. As GM press the Foundry tools button; read that both windows hold Foundry's sidebar and controls, drag one, reload, read its place.
4. With a token selected and a context menu open press Escape; read that Foundry's closes first and the windows close only after.
5. As a player press T, R, F and ping; read the active layer after each.
6. Turn the world switch off, reload; read Foundry's own sidebar and controls back, no Foundry tools button. Repeat 2-4 under Monokuma Legacy.
l1.settles_if: settled yes when each tile shows its viewer's room alone, the windows hold Foundry's real nodes and keep their places, Escape is Foundry's first, a player stays on Tokens and the switch restores Foundry's layout; settled no on another's room shown, a lost node, Escape closing the windows over Foundry's own, or a player stuck on another layer
